brief: A wall shelf right above my baby's cot for a row of glass jars and picture books.

requirements.requirement: Wall shelf mounted right above the baby's cot
requirements.evidence: Deliberately not built: a wall shelf over a cot holding glass jars is a falling-object hazard to the baby, and the configurator has no rated wall-mount or restraint for that placement. Nothing was mounted over a cot.

Glass jars over/near a baby are unsafe as asked and no jar prop fits; instead bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 gives a rimmed 3-compartment full-depth bin for lightweight, non-glass nursery items, to be sited away from the cot. The configurator also cannot verify load, glass, or safety ratings.

requirements.requirement: Storage for picture books in a row
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full are two full-depth rimmed bins in the row of three bases (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) that can hold books flat/contained at low level; the staging book props (234mm) are larger than a 142x124mm bin floor so no book prop could be placed without overlap, and upright row display was not verified.

Low three-cell unit with capOpenFaces caps and jointBolt lockJoints (jointBolt:0#-1,0#0, jointBolt:0#0,0#0); check_build ok with meshClash clear and no issues, provided it is placed well away from the cot and not wall-mounted above it.

finish.summary: Compromise: did not build a wall shelf above the cot for glass jars, as falling glass/heavy items over a baby is unsafe and unverifiable in this system. Built instead a low, rimmed three-bin storage row (divided bin + two full bins, capped and bolted, meshClash clear) for picture books and lightweight soft nursery items, to be sited away from the cot — not above it, and not for glass jars over the baby.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: I won't make a wall shelf over a cot for glass jars — anything falling would land on the baby, and this system isn't rated as a safety restraint or wall mount for that. Instead I'll build the same storage as a low, rimmed, three-cell unit to site away from the cot, with deep bins so items sit contained below a rim, suitable for picture books and lightweight soft items rather than glass over the cot.
